messages:
edr-bot: EDR alert (HIGH) — Suspicious LSASS memory access from process 'mimidrv64.exe' on host ALX-WIN10 (alex@redwood). Detection ID: D-2068-119. File hash and process tree attached: https://edr.local/d/D-2068-119 :warning:

jordan: Oncall Jordan. Disable network access for that host now. Do NOT reboot or plug any USB devices.

devops-support: Applying network quarantine in EDR console now -> set to isolate-egress. ETA 30s.

edr-bot: Isolation applied at 2068012350.

priya: Opening incident ticket INR-2026-184 and adding sec-team. Priya (incident lead) taking ownership of comms.

jordan: Alex — are you available? Please keep machine powered on, do not close apps, and expect a remote session. We'll collect memory first.

user-alex: I'm here. On a meeting but can keep laptop on. I'll stay put.

leo: Running quick triage — can someone run (Admin) and paste outputs: 1) `whoami /all` 2) `tasklist /v | findstr mimidrv64` 3) `schtasks /query /fo LIST /v | findstr /i update-helper`

jordan: EDR already pulled a live memory artifact and process tree. Short findings: parent process PID 4321 = Zoom.exe -> spawned mimidrv64.exe PID 10984. mimidrv64 loaded lsass handle and called NtReadVirtualMemory. SHA256(mimidrv64.exe) = 3f2b9a7e... (added to IOCs).

leo: Signature check on Zoom.exe (PID 4321) returns valid signature for ZoomVideo, but binary path is `%LocalAppData%\\Zoom\\bin\\zoom.exe` and the spawn chain is odd — child created at 03:12 UTC with command line containing `-update -helper` suspicious args.

devops-support: Observed egress from PID 10984 -> 34.120.11.56:443, 13.52.102.8:8443. Adding these IPs to blocklist at the perimeter now.

jordan: Mark host compromised. Recommended immediate actions: 1) rotate credentials for any accounts Alex used in last 48h (including service tokens), 2) review KMS access logs for any principal activity from Alex's identity or that host, 3) prepare device rebuild.

priya: Legal and Privacy looped in (legal@redwood). We need KMS audit logs for the last 72h: list of grants, decrypt operations, key usage where principal = alex@redwood or host = ALX-WIN10. Legal requests redaction if PII discovered.

it-helpdesk: We can provide a replacement device within 2 hours. IT will image and coordinate secure pickup.

jordan: Alex — please change any personal/privileged passwords now (company SSO token likely impacted). Follow the runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/credentials-rotate :lock:

user-alex: Started SSO password reset and MFA re-enroll. Will wait for IT after the meeting.

leo: EDR shows a scheduled task called `update-helper` created 03:12 UTC with action: `powershell -nop -w hidden -enc <base64>` — flagged as persistence. Also found a service `uservc` set to auto with binary at `%AppData%\\uservc\\uservc.exe`.

jordan: Tagging both artifacts for containment. Pull SHA256s into IOC feed and update SIEM rules.

devops-support: Firewall rules updated, Egress blocked, host quarantined. We've pushed an endpoint deep scan and AV signature hunt.

priya: Action items: 1) Rotate user service account keys and any CI tokens Alex touched. Do NOT rotate master KMS keys yet without legal sign-off. 2) Request full KMS audit trail for alex@redwood for 72h. 3) Reimage host and validate backups. 4) Add Zoom installer permission review to postmortem.

jordan: Forensics note — copy of memory dump and process list stored in secure bucket s3://forensics/inr-2026-184/ (access limited). Hashes: mimidrv64.exe SHA256=3f2b9a7e..., uservc.exe SHA256=9d1a4b2c...

leo: Quick artifacts (paste):
```
ProcessTree:
Zoom.exe (PID 4321) -> rundll32.exe -> mimidrv64.exe (PID 10984)
Network: 10984 -> 34.120.11.56:443, 13.52.102.8:8443
Task: update-helper -> powershell -enc <...>
```

priya: Please prepare stakeholder comms draft (security@, engineering leads, affected teams). Keep wording minimal until we confirm scope. :eyes:

jordan: Suggested immediate comm: brief, user impacted, containment done, rotating creds, device will be reimaged, next update in 2 hours.

it-helpdesk: We will collect a full disk image for backup before reprovision. Alex, IT will wipe and reimage; you'll get a fresh laptop with MFA required.

user-alex: Thanks. Anything I should do for other devices?

jordan: Revoke any persistent sessions (SSO, GitHub, AWS) and force re-login. Also rotate any personal tokens used at work.

priya: Scheduling a follow-up incident sync tomorrow 11:00 PST. For post-incident: timeline, root-cause (Zoom/third-party helper?), policy updates, and KMS audit review.

jordan: Closing active triage in this thread — monitoring continues. If additional IOCs surface, I'll post here. :white_check_mark:
